name: Straddle / Strangle Recentering Roll (Rolling the Untested Side In)
summary: When one side of a short premium structure is tested, close the untested side and re-sell it closer to the money in the same expiry, collecting extra credit and pulling the position's delta back toward neutral - the primary short-premium adjustment in the standard references.

legs.strike_rule: CLOSE the untested short call (buy to close) - shown for a put-side-tested position
RE-SELL a call at delta 0.25-0.30 in the SAME expiry, closer to spot than the one just closed
legs.dte_rule: the same expiry - recentering never changes the expiry

legs.strike_rule: If the base structure is defined-risk, also roll its long wing to (new short strike + W) so the wing stays attached
The tested short put is LEFT ALONE by this adjustment - recentering does not touch the tested side

max_profit: Original credit plus the recentering credit, if the underlying finishes between the new strikes
max_loss: Unchanged on the tested side; INCREASED on the recentered side, because the new short is closer to spot. For a defined-risk base: (width x 100) - cumulative credit on either side.
breakevens: Tested side unchanged; the other side moves in to the new short strike + cumulative credit per share

greeks.delta: pulled back toward zero - the purpose of the adjustment
greeks.gamma: more negative than before; the position is now tighter around spot

typical_dte: Applied with 14-35 DTE remaining; never inside 10 DTE
when_to_use: A short strangle, iron condor or iron butterfly has been tested on one side, the thesis is still range-bound, and the untested side has decayed to almost nothing. Recentering converts that dead premium into new credit and reduces directional exposure - but it narrows the profit range at exactly the moment the market is proving it can move.
entry_rules: ELIGIBILITY GATE - all must hold: (1) the untested short has lost >= 70% of its original premium; (2) the tested short's |delta| is between 0.25 and 0.40 (below that, do nothing; above that, defend the tested side instead); (3) >= 14 DTE remain; (4) the recentering can be done for a net credit.
ONE RECENTERING PER POSITION. Repeated recentering is how a neutral position becomes a naked directional one.
The new short strike must remain OUTSIDE the underlying's remaining expected move to expiry, and no closer than 0.30 delta.

The new short strikes must not cross: for a strangle the call strike must stay above the put strike (crossing them creates a short guts with a completely different risk profile, which is a separate structure and a separate decision).

DEFINED-RISK REQUIREMENT: if the base structure is an iron condor or butterfly, the long wing on the recentered side MUST be rolled with it in the same order. A short moved without its wing is a naked leg, which this account cannot carry.
Never recenter into an earnings date or a scheduled macro event inside the remaining life.
Execute as one MLeg order; if it must be legged, close the old short first and confirm before selling the new one.
management_rules: Treat the recentered structure as a new position: profit target 50% of CUMULATIVE credit, loss stop 2x cumulative credit, time stop at 21 DTE or the original time stop, whichever is sooner.
Do NOT also roll the tested side in the same action - defending the tested side and recentering the untested side are two different decisions and doing both at once produces an unanalyzable position.
If the underlying reverses after recentering and now tests the NEW short, close the whole structure. It has been given its one adjustment.
Log the recentering with the cumulative credit and the new, narrower profit range; the narrowed range is the cost and must be visible in the record.
exit_rules: Force-close the whole structure by 15:45 ET on expiration day.
Close any short at extrinsic < $0.10, |delta| >= 0.85, or ITM by more than 0.25 x its wing width.
Ex-dividend guard on any short call before every ex-date while ITM.
Abort mid-adjustment if the new short cannot be sold within 5 minutes of the old one being closed - a one-sided position with a live wing is acceptable for minutes, not for a session.
If both sides end up tested, close everything; a recentered position that is tested on both sides has no good outcome left.
assignment_risk: The adjustment itself briefly changes which legs are live, and on a defined-risk base a short can exist without its wing if the order is legged carelessly. After recentering, the closer short strike means a higher probability of finishing ITM, so the assignment probability of the whole structure has gone UP, not down - the delta improvement is not a safety improvement.
buying_power: For a defined-risk base, the requirement may rise if the recentered side's width changes; for a naked base (level 4, not permitted here) the margin is recomputed at the new strike.
liquidity_needs: Same expiry, two or three strikes, OI >= 250 each; recentering usually happens on a day the chain is already moving.
common_mistakes: Recentering for extra credit when the real problem is the tested side; recentering more than once; crossing the strikes into an inverted position without recognizing it as a different structure; moving a short without its wing; treating the improved delta as reduced risk when the profit range has narrowed.
zero_dte_notes: Not appropriate - at 0DTE the correct response to a tested side is to close, not to adjust.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
